sentence: This project uses machine learning on health records to build a rule that helps clinicians spot fractures caused by abuse in young children.
This project tests treatments for neuroblastoma in mouse models to learn how genetic and metabolic factors affect immune system and tumor interactions.
This project studies how a chemokine helps tumor cells hold back the immune system in neuroblastoma.
This project collects several kinds of data to study how brain systems interact to help individuals resist the effects of stress.
This project tries to attack the stem cells behind acute myeloid leukemia by blocking a step in how these cells produce energy.
This project combines deep learning with MRI methods to build imaging tools that detect nerve injury and demyelination in progressive multiple sclerosis.
This project studies how people separate and recognize speech from background noise, using behavior, brain activity and computer models.
This project builds heart MRI methods, without invasive procedures, to diagnose and monitor coronary microvascular dysfunction.
This project studies how mosquito biting times and places, and vector control tools, affect the spread of malaria.
This project tries to find animal viruses that could spread to humans and studies how and why they evolved traits that allow it.
This project develops prodrugs cleaved by singlet oxygen as a treatment for non-muscle invasive bladder cancer.
This project tests gene editors that use CRISPR to change a gene, aiming at a therapy for Alzheimer's disease.
This project studies how race-related stress affects stress and craving in African American people with alcohol use disorder, using laboratory tests.
This project studies whether blood cells with clonal hematopoiesis show different epigenetic and gene activity patterns that may raise cardiovascular disease risk.
This project builds computer models of heart fibroblasts to predict which patients will develop more fibrosis and which will respond to therapies.
This project develops a gene therapy carried by lipid nanoparticles, not opioids, to treat acute focal pain, testing it in human organoid and mouse models.
This project studies whether depleting heat shock transcription factors can treat acute myeloid leukemia by disrupting tumor metabolism and boosting immune attack.
This project provides imaging of cancer in rodent models and humans, including PET tracers, to track how tumors respond to treatment.
This project builds a very sensitive DNA test to detect circulating tumor DNA in blood and applies it to esophageal cancer patients.
This project looks for tissue biomarkers that show which patients with metastatic renal cell carcinoma will benefit from immune checkpoint inhibitor therapies.
